name: Physics
boundaries: Physics: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.original_title: A consistent, testable theory of quantum gravity, or a full theory of everything
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part, and not added as its own entry. The accessible laboratory claim is PHY-03. The information question is PHY-11. A single framework that also fixes every coupling, removes the Big Bang singularity, and enables wormholes or new energy sources has no one completion test. Those downstream uses are not supported as direct consequences.

original_dispositions.original_title: Direct detection and identification of the dark-matter particle
Microscopic explanation of dark energy and the cosmological-constant problem
original_dispositions.reason: Covered by PHY-05. The historical mismatch figure and the hope of manipulating vacuum energy were not carried into the entry.

original_dispositions.original_title: Resolution of the black-hole information paradox
Experimental confirmation of supersymmetry, or another solution to the hierarchy problem
original_dispositions.reason: Added as PHY-12, narrowed to the Higgs-mass mechanism. A generic demand for superpartners, an anthropic landscape, and the separate “why is gravity so weak” question were not added.

original_dispositions.original_title: Detection of primordial B-mode gravitational waves confirming cosmic inflation
original_dispositions.reason: A tensor spectrum would be a deep measurement inside a framework already used to interpret the cosmic microwave background. It would not by itself create a new principle or a new capability. A multiverse is a further inference. Zebrowski et al., arXiv:2601.20958, submitted 28 January 2026, https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20958, report in the arXiv HTML section “Upper limits on Early Causal Tensors” that a joint fit to BICEP/Keck, SPTpol, SPT-3G, Planck, and WMAP finds “no statistically-significant detection of either r or r_ect,” with 95% limits r_ect < 0.0077 and r < 0.033. That r limit is a preprint joint fit with causal tensor sources, not an official BICEP/Keck-only result, and it is not a detection.

original_dispositions.original_title: Complete, testable mechanism for matter–antimatter asymmetry
Fundamental resolution of the arrow of time
original_dispositions.reason: The low entropy of the early universe is a real conceptual problem. No missing experiment, new conservation law, or operable capability was specified beyond what a future initial-condition statement inside PHY-11 or PHY-05 might contain. An important unsolved problem by itself stays below the bar used here.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Initial compilation, 2026-11-01, selected PHY-01 through PHY-10.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: This revision, same cutoff, reconciles that list with the historical ten-item prompt.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PHY-01, PHY-02, PHY-03, PHY-06, PHY-07, PHY-09, and PHY-10 are retained. Their identities, completion standards, and source base are unchanged.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Overlaps are now flagged in the text: metallic hydrogen stays inside PHY-01; PHY-03 is separated from black-hole information; PHY-06 is separated from proton decay.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PHY-04 is amended by adding the Planck 2018 abstract densities. The cold-dark-matter density is about five times the baryon density in that fit.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical “about 85 percent of the matter” figure is not quoted, because that percentage was not a sentence in the abstract that was read. A possible identity overlap with a stable superpartner is flagged and left as two entries.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PHY-05 is amended so the historical 10^{-120} mismatch is explicitly a regularization-dependent estimate, using Martin and Kaya and Lahey, which the first pass already cited.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Manipulation of vacuum energy is stated as a further breakthrough, not a direct consequence.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PHY-08 is amended in its current state. The December 2025 KamLAND-Zen combination, T1/2 > 3.8 × 10^26 yr and 28–122 meV, is a stronger published limit than the germanium combination of 1.9 × 10^26 yr. The first-pass germanium result remains. The decay is still unobserved.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The problem statement no longer reads as if the germanium mass window were the global best.

The historical information-paradox item is a distinct principle from the tabletop gravity witness. Penington’s Page curve is a holographic calculation, and a 2025 review still records no experimental verification. Unsupported consequences in the historical blurb, including wormholes and new energy sources, are omitted.

reconciliation_change_log.change: PHY-12 is added in narrowed form. The concept is the measured physics that sets the Higgs-mass term. Supersymmetry is the concrete experimental target.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Constantin, Kraml, and Mahmoudi document the absence of superpartners and the survival of high-scale supersymmetry beyond feasible colliders. The weakness of gravity relative to other forces is not folded into this entry. Dark-matter candidacy is flagged as PHY-04.

The baryon density is already measured; the missing revolution is the mechanism plus a second observable. Electroweak baryogenesis remains unconfirmed and experimentally pressured. Proton decay and lepton-number violation stay separate entries.
